services.name: IAuditService
methods: record(actorId, action, entityType, entityId, oldState, newState)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: leave-type + leave-status + audit-log
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules. leave-type and leave-status are pure enums/models. audit-log is the cross-cutting audit service required by GP-002; it has no leave-domain dependencies and must exist before any state-changing operation is built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Policy & Balance: leave-policy + leave-balance
recommended_phases.rationale: Both depend only on leave-type (Phase 1). leave-policy defines the rules (max days per type, carry-over). leave-balance tracks per-employee balances. These are the domain rules engine that leave-request will validate against.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Core: leave-request (service + controller + routes)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior phases. This is the main application module: submit, approve, reject, cancel. It orchestrates policy validation, balance checks, status transitions, and audit recording. Contains the HTTP layer (controller + routes) since it's the only module with external-facing endpoints.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: leave-type and leave-status are domain-layer enums/models (innermost). leave-policy and leave-balance are domain services with repository interfaces (domain layer). leave-request is the application service orchestrating domain services, plus the presentation layer (controller + routes). audit-log is a cross-cutting infrastructure concern. Dependencies flow strictly inward: leave-request → {leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-status, leave-type, audit-log}; leave-policy → {leave-type}; leave-balance → {leave-type}; audit-log, leave-type, leave-status have zero deps. No circular dependencies. All state-changing operations in leave-request go through IAuditService.record() per GP-002. RBAC enforcement (GP-005) is applied at the route/controller level in leave-request. Input validation (GP-003) is applied at the controller boundary. All database access is through repository interfaces (GP-001).
